result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B keeps every question on real past events, including the last rental, a time something went wrong and the last time they compared places. It also has a fuller consent checklist and a 'Don't' list that targets hypotheticals and leading wording. A is well organized and its times add up, but its 'Tools & expectations' section asks a hypothetical about what renters would expect online. Each opening misses one required point: A never says the participant isn't being tested, and B never says the interviewer isn't selling anything. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A keeps every question tied to real past experience and has no leading or hypothetical prompts. Its spoken intro covers consent, recording and 'I'm not testing you', but it never tells the participant 'I'm not selling anything' (it only reminds the interviewer not to pitch). B's intro says 'not selling anything' and asks to record, but section 4 opens with the leading 'most annoying or confusing part', and section 5 asks hypothetical expectation questions and invites showing Paddlepoint. Both time plans add up to 40 minutes. B's two-column layout is denser and looks likely to run past one printed page.
